topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture, providing context on the complexity and immunological importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and central mechanism of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core principles, nomenclature rules, and the central role of C3 cleavage in complement function.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical recognition pathways that initiate complement and drive it toward an activation threshold on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream biological mechanisms through which activated complement targets and destroys pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct medical pathologies and infection risks that result from genetic or acquired complement deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary strategies and specific molecular mechanisms pathogens use to resist complement activity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the discussion on complement and outlines the topic for the subsequent lecture.
